entries.title: Psalms 90:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thou - Thou hadst thy power, and all thy perfections, from all eternity.

entries.title: Psalms 90:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Turnedst - But as for man, his case is far otherwise, though he was made by thee happy. and immortal, yet for his sin thou didst make him mortal and miserable. Saidst - Didst pronounce that sad sentence, return, O men, to the dust out of which ye were taken, Gen 3:19.

entries.title: Psalms 90:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Past - Indeed time seems long when it is to come, but when it is past, very short and contemptible. A watch - Which lasted but three or four hours.

entries.title: Psalms 90:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Them - Mankind. Away - Universally, without exception or distinction. A sleep - Short and vain, as sleep is, and not minded 'till it be past.

entries.title: Psalms 90:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Are consumed - Thou dost not suffer us to live so long as we might by the course of nature.

entries.title: Psalms 90:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hast set - Thou dost observe them, as a righteous judge, and art calling us to an account for them. Secret sins - Which though hid from the eyes of men, thou hast brought to light by thy judgments.

entries.title: Psalms 90:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Our years - Of the generality of mankind, in that and all following ages, some few persons excepted. Flee - We do not now go to death, as we do from our very birth, but flee swiftly away like a bird, as this word signifies.

entries.title: Psalms 90:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thy fear - According to the fear of thee; according to that fear which sinful men have of a just God. So - It bears full proportion to it, nay indeed doth far exceed it.

entries.title: Psalms 90:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Teach us - To consider the shortness of life, and the certainty and speediness of death. That - That we may heartily devote ourselves to true wisdom.

entries.title: Psalms 90:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Return - To us in mercy. How long - Will it be before thou return to us? Repent thee - Of thy severe proceedings against us.

entries.title: Psalms 90:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The beauty - His gracious influence, and glorious presence. In us - Do not only work for us, but in us,
